industry.why: Overweight, carried unchanged and better supported. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses now name staples as the place to be, Jefferies' desk (17 Oct) favouring 'pricing-power defensives such as staples and utilities' as energy inflation seeps into core goods and Danske (18 Oct) calling them 'not a bad place to hide'; energy, utilities and staples led the week and European defensives beat cyclicals by 4.7 points over four weeks (37-breadth-and-defensives.md). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: C now, D prior, so the market has started to pay. Not Double Overweight: the multiples that make staples defensive derate with a 5.10% ten-year, and a defensive destination four weeks into a rotation is a crowded one. The sector rows carry B on Beverages, Tobacco, Household products, Food retail and Food production. Moves to A if defensives lead for a second month with the industry's relative strength at B or better.

sector.why: Overweight, carried, with its condition tested. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, F prior; the 16-Oct-26 reading was C, so the grade slipped one step in the week, short of the condition written on the row (back to C if relative strength returns to F). Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Jefferies' desk call for 'pricing-power defensives' covers staples broadly, low-volatility and dividend stocks outperformed (Goldman, 19 Oct), and tobacco remains the archetype of the simple, proven, high-cash-yield case Richard's line says investors crowd to; no source named tobacco. Counter-case: six stocks, the slip, and regulatory risk; back to C if the next reading is F.

geography.why: Neutral, from Overweight. Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): the condition written on this row on 2-Oct-26 (it stays B only while the Banks row is Overweight) is no longer met, since Banks goes to Neutral on the credit tripwire; the Greek listings in the MI Pool are six banks plus Cenergy, HELLENiQ Energy and Motor Oil, with the live holding Ballys Intralot beside them, so the country letter was a second bank weight, and in a week when European sovereign stress is spreading from France to Italy and Spain a bank-heavy periphery listing is where contagion lands next, though Greek spreads themselves were not read. Relative strength is not graded by country. Counter-case: Goldman Sachs's emerging market team (8 Oct) stays overweight Greece by name, Greece is not among the sovereigns named under stress, and the Greek energy names are on the right side of the regime; back to B if the Banks row returns to Overweight.
